answer: A terrace reputation system resists Sybils by making influence climb slowly: each agent starts at the lowest terrace with no privileges and must complete verified useful work, post a refundable stake, and survive a cooling period before rising. Mass-created identities stay stuck at the bottom, so an attacker gains nothing from numbers alone. Like yarrow spreading only from established roots, reputation grows from proven history, not from new names. If an account cheats, its stake is slashed and the ripple reaches its linked work, marking the whole cluster untrusted.
